hook.text: Electronics that dissolve when their job is done — biodegradable devices disappear inside the body, no surgery to remove.

buildup.text: Transient electronics use silk, magnesium, and silicon nanomembranes — materials that dissolve safely in body fluids.

discovery.text: A biodegradable pressure sensor tracked brain swelling post-surgery — then dissolved harmlessly over weeks, avoiding removal.

twist.text: Controlling dissolution rate is tricky — the device must last long enough to be useful but dissolve before causing complications.

climax.text: Eco-friendly transient electronics could reduce e-waste — devices that return to the environment instead of filling landfills.

punchline.text: Use it and lose it — biodegradable electronics vanish when their job is done.

quiz.question: What is the main engineering challenge for biodegradable electronics?
options: They cannot conduct electricity as well as conventional electronics
Controlling the dissolution rate so devices last long enough to function but dissolve before causing harm
The materials are too expensive to manufacture at scale
